definitions.explanation: The moral standards and behavioral norms of a community, school, or organization. Often appears in discussions about maintaining or disrupting order.

examples.japanese: {風紀|ふうき}を{乱|みだ}す{行為|こうい}だ。
examples.english: That's behavior that disrupts public morals.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}の{風紀|ふうき}{委員|いいん}に{選|えら}ばれた。
examples.english: I was chosen as a member of the school's discipline committee.

examples.japanese: {社内|しゃない}の{風紀|ふうき}が{乱|みだ}れているので、{服装|ふくそう}{規定|きてい}を{見直|みなお}すことになった。
examples.english: Since workplace discipline has deteriorated, it was decided to review the dress code.

notes:
Frequently appears in school and workplace contexts. Japanese schools often have a {風紀|ふうき}{委員|いいん} (discipline committee) or {風紀|ふうき}{委員長|いいんちょう} (head of the discipline committee) — students responsible for enforcing rules on uniforms, behavior, etc. A common trope in anime and manga.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風紀|ふうき}を{乱|みだ}す (disrupt public morals/discipline)
- {風紀|ふうき}を{正|ただ}す (correct/restore discipline)
- {風紀|ふうき}{委員|いいん} (discipline committee member)
- {風紀|ふうき}{委員長|いいんちょう} (head of discipline committee)
- {風紀|ふうき}の{取|と}り{締|し}まり (enforcement of discipline)
